possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card only states it is a mergekit SLERP merge of two named models with no architecture, training data, or evaluation details, so inner workings and design/evaluation process are undocumented.

possible_risks.description: Data provenance refers to the traceability of data (including synthetic data), which includes its ownership, origin, transformations, and generation. Proving that the data is the same as the original source with correct usage terms is difficult without standardized methods for verifying data sources or generation.
possible_risks.justification: As a merge of two pre-trained models, the card gives no information about the provenance or traceability of the underlying training data used by the base models.

possible_risks.description: Lack of data transparency might be due to insufficient documentation of training or tuning dataset details, including synthetic data generation.
possible_risks.justification: The card does not document training or tuning dataset details for the merged model or its components, only names the merged models.

possible_risks.description: The content of the training data used for generating the model's output is not accessible.
possible_risks.justification: Because the card provides no training-data content or source information for the merged components, outputs cannot be traced back to specific training data.

possible_risks.description: Since foundation models can be used for many purposes, a model's intended use is important for defining the relevant risks of that model. As the use changes, the relevant risks might correspondingly change.
possible_risks.justification: The card only labels the model as a language model merge and gives no intended-use or downstream-task definition, leaving relevant risks undefined.
